background.evidence: Named company, named role, six years, and the exact scope of what he owned.

connection.evidence: Dated incident, a euro figure, and a personal consequence he had to carry.

essential.evidence: Cost of failure is clear and attributed. Downstream risk beyond money is not developed.

spread.evidence: Segment is described but the number of companies in it is never derived.

icp.evidence: Role, geography, staff band, shipment volume, and the budget line it comes out of.

pain.evidence: Hours, error rate, average value, monthly total, and fourteen months of his own tracking.

existingAttempts.evidence: Names CargoWise and Transporeon, the Excel fallback, and the offshore bookkeeper workaround.

limitations.evidence: Structural reason the incumbents stop, plus why they have no incentive to fix it.

solution.evidence: One screen, one job, explicitly nothing else in v1. Vague on how the matching itself works.

boundary.evidence: Nothing else in version one, stated outright. The scan-matching case is in, everything adjacent is deferred.

falsifiable.evidence: If fewer than two of three pilots convert by December, he stops and re-scopes. Named threshold, named date, losing outcome.

validation.evidence: Three signed paid pilots by name, a manually delivered version, and fourteen interviews.

distribution.evidence: Named network and a specific channel, but no first target named.

nextSteps.evidence: Dated, priced, named partners, and an explicit kill criterion.

reasons: B2B, sold to a freight operations manager with a finance director holding the budget.
First market is the Netherlands and Belgium.
Founder is full time on it.
The document extraction and matching is the product, not a feature bolted on.
